Hi Michael / Procurement team — thanks for the clear questions. Answers below and a proposed MAP. Short version: we can support quarterly invoicing via Redwood's finance + AWS private offer activation, but it requires a short payment SOW and the buyer CFO sign-off for the private offer activation when the value crosses your internal threshold.

Details:
- Buyer approvals: For AWS private offers our activation checklist includes an evidence pack (SOC2 summary, data handling statement, product security brief, and a short customer use-case statement). When the deal size is >$100k ARR we ask for an exec sign-off (CFO or authorized finance delegate). If you want to expedite, include a one-paragraph CFO waiver request in the PO attachment and we can route for a "fast-track" review.

- Payment cadence: We do support quarterly invoicing (NET45) for Marketplace private-offer activations, but it is treated as a billing amendment to the private offer and requires: (a) Redwood SOW signed, (b) finance contact for invoicing, and (c) explicit billing cadence noted in the AWS private offer metadata. If quarterly invoice terms are required, we will attach a short SOW and run the activation after the CFO sign-off. Note that choosing 24 months will lengthen internal approval; 12 months is typically faster.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) We send an evidence pack + SOW template (attached) — Alex to upload.
2) Finovate confirms preferred term (12m) and supplies CFO approver email + billing contact.
3) Redwood creates AWS private offer draft, attaches SOW and evidence pack, and submits for Finovate signature.
4) Once CFO signs (or approves waiver), Redwood triggers activation with quarterly invoicing metadata.

Attachments referenced: Finovate_Evidence_Pack_v1.zip (SOC2 summary, security brief), Finovate_SOW_v2.pdf (billing cadence clause included).

If this looks right I can loop in Finance (jordan) and Legal (laura) to confirm the SOW language.
